content: Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital is recognized as one of the leading academic medical centers in the United States, offering advanced, state-of-the-art care across a comprehensive range of healthcare services. Its specialties include cardiac care, encompassing everything from screening to heart surgery and transplantation, cancer care, emergency medicine, pediatrics, and maternal-fetal medicine. The hospital serves as a central provider of healthcare services, medical education, and clinical research in Central New Jersey. It is a clinical campus for the Robert Wood Johnson Medical School in New Brunswick and provides training programs for medical students, residents, fellows, nurses, and allied health professionals across various specialties. The mission of Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital is to improve the health status of the region's population by delivering appropriate healthcare and medical services. To achieve this, the hospital functions as a primary site for physician education, offers programs in allied and community health education, and provides highly complex healthcare resources to support the educational process. The hospital offers clinical programs in areas such as diabetes self-management education, digestive disorders, neurology (including a Clinical Neurosciences Center and a Parkinson's Disease Information and Referral Center), radiology (including a Women's Imaging Center), sleep disorders, and various surgical specialties (including bloodless surgery, cardiothoracic, orthopedic, prostate cancer, thoracic, and vascular surgery). It also provides transplantation services for heart, kidney, and pancreas, as well as trauma and emergency medicine services, including a Level I Trauma Center, Stroke Center, and injury prevention programs. Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital maintains three Centers of Excellence: the Cardiovascular Center of Excellence, the Cancer Center of Excellence, and the Women’s and Children’s Center of Excellence. Additionally, it operates the Bristol-Myers Squibb Children’s Hospital, which includes specialized units such as the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), Pediatric Emergency Department, Pediatric Unit, Adolescent Unit, Hematology/Oncology Unit, and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). The hospital is the principal teaching hospital for the University of Medicine and Dentistry of New Jersey (UMDNJ) Robert Wood Johnson Medical School, which is the largest health sciences school of its kind in the United States. UMDNJ is also New Jersey's leading research university, surpassing other major research institutions in the state, such as Princeton University and Rutgers University, in research grant funding. The university maintains various academic partnerships with other institutions in New Jersey. The origins of Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital date back to 1885, when it was established as the New Brunswick City Hospital. In 1888, the directors raised $3,000 to purchase land for the John Wells Memorial Hospital. It was renamed Middlesex General Hospital in 1916 and later became Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital in 1986. The Robert Wood Johnson Health Network comprises some of the best healthcare providers in New Jersey, including leading academic centers, acute care facilities, a university of health sciences, and top research hospitals. The network offers a wide spectrum of healthcare services, ranging from traditional hospital-based specialties to social services and dental care. It is the only health network in New Jersey with a medical school as a partner, as well as a senior service organization providing long-term care and assisted living facilities. Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital is one of the few hospitals in the nation to offer the first fully implantable artificial heart, as identified by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The hospital, along with Johns Hopkins Hospital in Maryland and Jewish Hospital in Louisville, Kentucky, has been selected as one of the initial sites for this groundbreaking technology. The hospital has been recognized for its patient safety initiatives, including receiving Magnet Designation for nursing excellence for the third consecutive time. Former RWJUH President and CEO Clifton R. Lacy, MD, was ranked among Modern Physician Magazine's 50 Most Powerful Physician Executives in 2005 and 2006, as well as Modern Healthcare Magazine's 100 Most Powerful People in Healthcare in 2005. RWJUH was the only hospital in New Jersey to rank in the top ten percent for both heart attack and pneumonia treatment for two consecutive years, according to the New Jersey Department of Health and Senior Services' annual state report on hospital quality.
